statement: The warning line and refuse-by-default results measured on the 1.7B (WARNCAL precision 0.39, recall 0.67, P(correct|warned) 0.05) hold for the 4B and for Gemma E2B on the same MAIN 97 K0 traces: precision >= 0.30, recall >= 0.55, P(correct|warned) <= 0.10. If so, the refuse-by-default + show-anyway note applies to the maintainer's actual default, not only to the 1.7B entry.
why_now: The refuse-by-default note (P5 send 2) is built on 1.7B evidence, but the RC ships the 4B, which declines 0 % on the phone (SPEED-PRECHECK) and reads packs better (PACKREAD). Its CEs may move into cited, unwarned answers, as the 1.7B's did on the pack-matched set (precision 0.22 there). Sending a note calibrated on the wrong model is the main honesty risk in the maintainer package.
method: 0-LLM. Reuse tools/warncal_showanyway.py unchanged (sha 8e162cea) with the 4B K0 s42 and Gemma K0 MAIN 97 traces (VS4B, GEMMA4 stage 2) and their existing Haiku-low judgments. Freeze an addendum to criterion d641551b first. Report the same table (precision, recall, P(corr|w), P(corr|u), ratio, reveal correct:CE, health reveals) per model, with item-cluster CIs. Add the Pixel 4B final-cut7-v01 57 as a replication if the warning reason codes are in its receipts.
ceiling: Pass/fail on the note's scope. A precision difference of about 0.15 between models is detectable at about 250 answers per model. It feeds the note's wording directly.
kill_criterion: If the 4B's warning precision has CI-high < 0.30, or recall < 0.50, or P(correct|warned) > 0.15, the note says refuse-by-default is validated for the 1.7B only. For the 4B default it recommends 'show with the warning line' (current behaviour), not hiding. The claim's honesty section then names the model every number comes from.
lens: Honesty and the product that s

statement: On identical items, refuse-by-default changes the default-tier choice. Data: MAIN 97 K0 desktop judged traces for the 1.7B, Gemma E2B and 4B (GEMMA-VS-4B), plus the 57 Pixel parity ids (gemma73-a and final-cut7-v01 judged; q17b73-a if judged). Under refuse-by-default, the 1.7B shows at least 3 fewer confident errors per 100 questions than the 4B (CE-shown/100), and its correct-shown/100 is no more than 5 below the 4B's. Under show-all, the 4B dominates on both. If so, the maintainer note can say: 1.7B + refuse-by-default = the honest fast default; 4B = the more-complete default with more visible errors.
why_now: The maintainer's RC defaults to the 4B on 8 GB, and task #1 asks him to add a 1.7B entry. The only argument for the 1.7B so far is speed (SPEED-PRECHECK: all tiers USABLE) plus 1.7B-only honesty numbers. The default-tier recommendation has to go out before 10-23, and it needs one same-items table with correct-shown, CE-shown, declined, warned and p50 time per tier and mode.
method: 0-LLM. Freeze the criterion (sha) first. Per tier x mode (show-all; refuse-by-default = hide declined, warned or no-kept-source answers, the RU definition), count per 100 questions: correct-shown (corr >= 4), CE-shown (corr <= 1.5), partial-shown, hidden, and floor-adjusted U, from the existing Haiku-low judge.v1 judgments. Add p50 complete time from the Pixel traces. Item-cluster bootstrap (B 2000, seed 11) for paired tier differences. Report deterministic-pool ids separately (30/72 phone ids give identical text across tiers) so that the divergent ids carry the comparison. Script under ruler/tools, output ruler/TIER-PER100-2026-10-22.md + json.
cost: 0 judge, 0 generation, about 2 h coordinator/agent time
ceiling: A decision table, not a U lever. It decides the default-tier line of the maintainer notes and the claim's tier row. The CE-shown difference that matters (3 per 100) is resolvable at n 97 only if it is real; the CI is reported either way.
kill_criterion: Frozen rule. If, under refuse-by-default, the 4B's CE-shown/100 is within 3 of the 1.7B's (paired CI includes 0) and the 4B's correct-shown/100 is at least 5 higher, the 4B dominates. The note then recommends keeping the 4B default (refuse-by-default on) and frames the 1.7B entry only as the low-RAM/fast option. No 'more honest' wording for the 1.7B anywhere.
lens: Honesty and the product that s

statement: Gemma 4 E2B (thinking off, engine sampler) behind PR-1 (NUMGUARD r3 + HEALTHGAP r2) + WARN v2 is as safe as the 1.7B on health-shaped questions. On the LITESAFETY protocol (64 public safety probes + health-shaped v0.1 items), unsafe answers <= 1 (the 1.7B and 4B each had 1), every unsafe answer carries the warning, and 0 thinking markers appear. This is the T3 gate the plan sets for the Gemma opt-in entry.
why_now: P5 send 3 (the Gemma opt-in entry) is conditional on T1 thinking and T3 safety passing on 10-23, and neither has a QUEUE result. Gemma reveals more text than the 1.7B (it declines 0 %, refused 1/7 vs 4/7 in GEMMA4-PHONE), so it is the tier most exposed to unsafe health answers. Without this run the Gemma entry cannot be sent before the freeze.
method: Mini generation, 1 slot: Gemma E2B with the gemma4-e2b-engsamp patch on the LITESAFETY tree (be-cut7-warn) with the same adapter switch. Use the same 64 probes + health items. Skip ids whose answer comes from deterministic layers, which give byte-identical text across models, and reuse the 1.7B rows for those. Freeze an addendum to criterion b0cf5d5f before generation. Score with the LITESAFETY scorer (jev, capped, logged) plus a thinking-marker regex. Add a blind Opus safety audit only for answers the scorer flags, at most 20 calls. Run T1 (20 prompts, 0 thinking markers, bounded tokens) in the same pass.
cost: about 70-90 generations on 1 mini slot (< 1 h); jev < [usage detail removed]; <= 20 Opus audit calls; 0 Haiku
ceiling: A binary safety gate for one maintainer send, measured by the same protocol already accepted for the 1.7B and the 4B.
kill_criterion: Any of the following and the Gemma entry is not sent before the freeze, or is sent with health questions routed to the 1.7B/decline path if the RC can do that: unsafe answers >= 2; any unsafe answer without the warning; >= 1 thinking marker in T1 or T3; answers hitting the token cap on > 10 % of prompts.
lens: Honesty and the product that s

statement: The ruler can tell tiers apart; the 1.7B simply sits close to a closed-book 1.5B. On the v0.1 57 dev ids, with the 6 deterministic-layer items removed, 4B - 1.5B closed-book is >= +0.08 U with a CI low > +0.03, while 1.7B - 1.5B stays < 0.05. The 1.7B - 1.5B gap sits on items where the 1.7B kept a source: covered-minus-uncovered DiD > 0. Planned framing on the page: 'the 1B row is a level anchor; separability is a coverage property'. Without this check the page would report a failed separability gate.
why_now: Spec section 8 lists decline < 1B < B <= A-union < reference with non-overlapping CIs. FLOOR and JUDGE-V1_1 show the 1.7B failing that ordering on dev under two judges. Before R4 we must know which it is: a ruler with no resolution (the spec must state the MDE and drop the gate wording), or a product fact (report it as a level). Otherwise a sceptical reader of the 10-24 table will read 'not separable' as 'the ruler cannot see anything'.
method: 0-LLM. Freeze a criterion first. Use existing Haiku 5.5-low judge.v1 rows on the same 57 ids and the same references: 1.5B closed-book (FLOOR), 1.7B K0 control s42/s43, Gemma 4 E2B phone and the Pixel 4B cut 7 (GEMMA4-PHONE-JUDGE), and the 1.7B phone. Drop deterministic-v01.ids. Compute paired gaps vs the 1.5B with a cluster bootstrap, and split by kept_X from each arm's trace (covered vs uncovered) to get the DiD. Repeat under U_CU if RV1 passes, and under v1.1 for the 1.7B/1.5B pair, which already exists. Compute the analytic MDE at n 75 from the observed item SD for the R2 spec.
ceiling: Detects 4B - 1.5B >= 0.08, which is above the 0.05 MDE at n about 50. It decides the separability wording of spec section 8 and of the page.
kill_criterion: If the CI low of 4B - 1.5B is <= 0, the ruler lacks tier resolution at n about 57. In that case: the section 8 separability check becomes 'reported, not a gate' in the R2 spec, every R4 row prints the MDE (0.05 at n 50, 0.03 at n 97), and the page makes no 'decline < 1B < app' statement. If the covered-subset 1.7B - 1.5B is <= 0.05 or the DiD CI includes 0, drop the 'coverage explains the level' sentence and report the 1.7B as 'level with a closed-book 1.5B on dev, both judges'.

statement: How the 7/75 device-location (current-city) v0.4 items are handled cannot change the verdict. Their reference-mass share times the largest plausible app-U swing is <= 0.03 of U-total. The swing runs from 0 (the submitted APK has no places path, so it refuses or answers from memory) to the tile-path level measured on dev (VENUEGPS-2, v0.1 food/vx items with location + area tile). So the R2 spec can pre-register: scored as given in the headline (no exclusion), plus one labelled sensitivity row 'with device location + area tile (desktop runner, not the submitted APK)'.
why_now: TILE-PATH shows no phone app can run a current-city query today. Deciding exclusion after seeing R4 scores would be post-hoc stratum surgery, which a sceptical judge would reject. The rule must be inside the R2 sha (10-23), and the bound costs nothing.
method: 0-LLM. Freeze a criterion first. From INPACK-STRATUM (already exposed fields only: 7 items with lat/lon keys) and the v0.1 dev proxies (food-001/002/006, vx-003/4/5): (1) reference s share of the location items under the existing v1 references; (2) app U on those ids for three variants: the claim kit without location, kit-vgps2 with location + tile (VENUEGPS-2 rows), and a bare refusal (0 under the R4 rule). Project the swing in U-total at the v0.4 share (7/75, weighted by the dev reference-mass ratio), with a bootstrap over the dev ids. Do not read v0.4 question text, checklists or city values.
ceiling: Settles a pre-registration rule. It is a bound, not an effect, so MDE does not apply.
kill_criterion: If the projected swing CI high is > 0.03 of U-total, the current-city items become a separate pre-registered stratum. U-total is printed both with and without them, the verdict uses the 'with' version (scored as given, APK has no places path), and the claim text states in the headline row that the submitted app cannot answer current-city questions. If <= 0.03, they stay in the headline as given, with one sensitivity row.

statement: The self-test pack gain (+0.056 1.7B, +0.069 K3, +0.076/+0.102 Gemma) is a lexical artefact of pack-written questions. Self-test questions share far more surface tokens with their gold chunk than real questions do. Prediction: when the 180 self-tests are stratified by question-to-gold-chunk overlap (BM25 rank of the gold chunk for the raw question, plus token Jaccard), the K3-K0 gain in the lowest tertile is at most +0.02 with a CI that includes 0. Reweighting the self-tests to the real v0.1 overlap distribution brings the gain under +0.03.
why_now: The research-page outline still carries the self-test numbers (1.7B K3 +0.069, Gemma +0.102) as the pack thesis. INPACK-SPLIT and FACTPRESENT show they do not transfer. This 0-LLM test says whether any self-test number can be quoted at all, or must become a footnote, before the page freezes.
method: Freeze the criterion (sha) first: tertile cut points from the real-item overlap distribution, not the self-test one. For each of the 180 self-tests (gold = in_pack_facts chunk) and the 37 real v0.1 items with a Y/P gold (gold-labels.tsv), compute, read-only on the pack FTS: (a) the bm25 rank of the gold chunk for the raw question, (b) token Jaccard of question vs gold chunk after stopword removal, (c) rare-term overlap (tokens with IDF above the 90th percentile). Join to the existing LITEPACKS K0/K3 Haiku judgments (1.7B) and GEMMA-PACKS (Gemma). Report the stratified K3-K0 gain with item-clustered bootstrap CIs, plus an importance-weighted gain matched to the real-item overlap histogram. 0 LLM, 0 judge.
cost: 0 LLM, 0 judge, 0 paid; about 2 h on the MacBook (FTS queries over the installed packs plus a join to existing judgment JSONs).
ceiling: n/a (0-LLM analysis). It decides whether the self-test gain may appear on the page, and with which caveat.
kill_criterion: Kill the artefact explanation (the self-test gain stays quotable as 'single-fact retrieval-matched questions') if the lowest-overlap tertile still shows K3-K0 of at least +0.04 with a CI above 0, OR the real-distribution-reweighted gain is at least +0.04 with a CI above 0. Otherwise the page drops the self-test gain from the headline and reports it only as an upper bound with the overlap caveat.
lens: Packs and the RAG funnel. Wher

statement: Under A-union, at least 2 of the 6 text packs (prime suspect medlineplus, never retrieved; then visa or firstaid) contribute 0 kept chunks on every dev item: v0.1 57 + MAIN 97 + phone 73 + the 180 self-tests minus their own pack's items. Dropping them from the default persona set leaves the kept context byte-identical on at least 98 pct of dev items. It also saves at least 0.3 s of Pixel 8a retrieval p50, about 0.15 s per pack per question measured in AUNION-PIXEL.
why_now: AUNION-PIXEL measured a +2.4 s serial-search cost that is fixed per pack, not tied to size. The persona map is still a draft awaiting r4to's veto. A pack that never reaches the kept context is pure latency and download size. Before the 10-23 freeze this is a concrete maintainer note plus a page line ('what each pack actually contributes').
method: Freeze the criterion (sha) first. Replay the A-union kit with the RAG-FUNNEL logging patch: stub server, 0 generation, MacBook. Use the AUNION-PIXEL pack list and topK. Per item, log each pack's raw hits, its fusion rank, and whether any of its chunks survives the keep step. Tabulate kept-chunk contribution per pack. For each pack with 0 or 1 contributions, replay A-union minus that pack and diff the kept titles and context bytes. Estimate the latency saving from the per-pack SQL seconds in the aunion73-a trace (no new phone run needed for the decision; a confirmation run on a cool Pixel is optional). Separately record for medlineplus: on health items, does it hold a fact chunk that loses at fusion (rank inside its own list vs the fused cut)? That separates 'no content' from 'outranked'.
cost: 0 LLM, 0 judge; replay about 20-30 min on the MacBook plus 1 h of analysis; an optional 10-item Pixel confirmation run (cool phone, about 15 min).
ceiling: n/a for U, which is unchanged by design (kept context identical). Latency ceiling about 0.15 s x pruned packs per question; with 2-3 packs that is 0.3-0.45 s of the +2.4 s.
kill_criterion: Kill if every one of the 6 packs contributes kept chunks on at least 3 dev items, OR if removing any candidate pack changes the kept context on more than 2 pct of items. The default set then stays at 6, and the cost question moves entirely to PK-5.
lens: Packs and the RAG funnel. Wher

statement: The honesty numbers that claim v5 will quote from WARNCAL and SHOWANYWAY survive an Opus re-judge, as the gate number did (10->4 became 7->3). On a stratified sample of 1.7B MAIN 97 answers (40 warned, 40 unwarned shown, 30 revealable hidden), Opus judge.v1 gives warning precision >= 0.30, P(correct|warned) <= 0.10, and reveal correct:CE < 1.0. Haiku over-calls CE (CE-OPUS: 6/23; CE-OPUS-RU: 10 vs 7), so precision could drop and the show-anyway verdict could flip.
why_now: Claim v5 (10-25) quotes claim numbers from Opus only (P3 and the judge rule). Today the warning and show-anyway numbers exist only as Haiku labels. It is cheaper to re-judge existing answers now than to drop the sentences on 10-25. Haiku's known direction (over-calling CE) biases exactly these two numbers.
method: Judge only, 0 generation. Freeze the criterion (sha) and sample first: stratified by warned / unwarned-shown / revealable-hidden, seed fixed, MAIN 97 + ST-SE (no pack-matched self-tests, where the line already fails), preferring divergent-main ids to deterministic-layer answers. Opus judge.v1, both orders, N = 4 shards: 110 answers x 2 = 220 calls. Recompute precision, recall (sample-weighted), P(corr|w) and correct:CE among reveals with Haiku and Opus side by side, plus kappa. Same layout as CE-OPUS-RU.
cost: about 220 Opus calls (within the claim-number allowance), 0 Haiku, 0 generation
ceiling: Decides which honesty sentences enter claim v5 and with which judge named. Proportions at n 40 per stratum give CI half-widths of about 0.15, enough to test the 0.30 / 0.10 / 1.0 thresholds.
kill_criterion: If Opus warning precision has CI-high < 0.30, the claim drops 'the warning catches two-thirds of confident errors' and keeps only 'no source found'. If Opus P(correct|warned) > 0.15, the '5 % of warned answers are correct' sentence is dropped. If Opus reveal correct:CE has CI-low >= 1.0, HON-2's liability verdict is withdrawn and the note's show-anyway text is rewritten. Any of these is logged as a Haiku-vs-Opus disagreement in the honesty section.
lens: Honesty and the product that s

statement: Merging the A-union text packs into one format-2 sqlite cuts Pixel 8a retrieval p50 from about 3.9 s to at most 2.4 s (at least 1.5 s saved) with no loss in what reaches the model. The merge is one FTS5 table plus one embedding table, same bge-small embeddings, same chunk ids with a source column. The fused top-K keeps fact reach equal or better: RAG-FUNNEL S3+S4+S5 counts within ±1 item on K3-equivalent MAIN 97, kept-title parity at least 90 pct on the phone 73. Serial search is then a fixable engine detail, not a property of having packs.
why_now: The +2.4 s per question is the only measured product cost of packs (PSS flat), and it is what moved the 73-item run into the MARGINAL band. a competitor team ships a single 30 GB BM25 index. A one-file pack is a maintainer-actionable fix that needs no llama.cpp change and no new model, and it must be known before the ~10-23 freeze.
method: Freeze the criterion (sha) first: parity thresholds, latency threshold, cool-phone gate. Build boar-aunion-merged.sqlite on the mini from the 6 A-union packs: copy chunks with a pack-source column, rebuild FTS5, copy the vectors, and set the same embedding sha so packs.ts accepts it as one pack. Step 1 (0 LLM, MacBook): retrieval replay of the 73 phone items and MAIN 97 with merged vs serial A-union. Report kept-title parity and the funnel stage counts. Global BM25 IDF changes under the merge, which is the main risk to parity. Step 2, only if step 1 passes: push the merged pack to the Pixel 8a in place of the 6 files (gazetteer unchanged). Run the 1.7B on the 73 with a cool phone (thermal gate status 0, battery at most 31 C), same APK, and compare retrieval p50/p90, answer p50, TTFT and PSS against aunion73-a. Restore the A-union kit afterwards and verify the shas.
cost: 0 judge, 0 paid; merge build on the mini about 30-60 min (1 slot, no generation); MacBook replay about 30 min; Pixel run about 10 min plus kit push and restore (about 30 min); total under 1 day.
ceiling: Latency up to about 2.4 s retrieval p50 (the full serial overhead); U is expected unchanged. The parity gate stands in for a quality screen, so no judge is needed unless parity falls below 90 pct.
kill_criterion: Kill at step 1 if kept-title parity is below 90 pct on the phone 73, OR the merged funnel loses 2 or more items from S4+S5 on MAIN 97 (the IDF shift costs reach). Kill at step 2 if the Pixel retrieval p50 saving is under 1.0 s, OR PSS rises above 4.0 GB for the 1.7B. On kill, the maintainer note says 'keep the persona set small (see PK-4)' instead of 'ship one merged pack'.
lens: Packs and the RAG funnel. Wher

statement: judge.v1 does not need a prompt change to pass the decline check. FLOOR shows the leak sits only in the correctness dimension: completeness and usefulness are exactly 1.0 for all three decline variants. Proposed fix: compute U from completeness + usefulness only (U_CU) and keep correctness for the CE label only. Under that rule (a) all three decline variants score U 0, (b) system gaps (4B-1.7B, Gemma-1.7B, 1.7B-1.5B) move by less than 0.03 with no rank flip, and (c) item test-retest SD is at most judge.v1's 0.0206 on the same 20 ids. The CE labels cannot flip, because the correctness bytes and the CE rule are untouched. This beats both v1.1 (7 CE flips) and the alternative 'v1 + decline subtraction', U' = (U - U_dec)/(1 - U_dec). That alternative carries the decline arm's own CI (0.037-0.081) into every row.
why_now: R1 is decided at noon 10-23, and RULER-SPEC section 8 makes 'decline arm valid' a precondition of the verdict. v1.1 failed on CE flips and v1.1c may fail the same way. U_CU is the only fix left that keeps judge.v1's bytes and CE behaviour, and every number it needs already exists.
method: 0-LLM. Freeze a criterion (sha) first. Inputs, all existing Haiku 5.5-low judge.v1 rows (both orders), with per-dimension scores read by floor_agg.py: FLOOR decline a/b/c (30 ids); the v1 retest-20 repeats 1-2; MAIN 97 K0 for 1.7B, Gemma and 4B (GEMMA-VS-4B); and the v0.1 57 for the 1.5B closed-book and the 1.7B K0 control. Compute U_full, U_CU and U' (subtraction) per arm, the paired gaps with a cluster bootstrap, item-level Spearman U_CU vs U_full, and retest item SD under U_CU. Skip the deterministic ids (ruler/ids/deterministic-*.ids) for the SD and gap sensitivity rows. Report the same table for the Opus rows that exist (CE-OPUS-RU 38 answers) as a family check.
cost: 0 LLM, 0 judge, about 1 h coordinator script
ceiling: Decides the R4 judge without new calls. It is a validity gate, so MDE does not apply.
kill_criterion: Do NOT adopt U_CU if any of these holds: a decline variant's U CI high > 0.05; retest item SD under U_CU > 0.0206; any pairwise system gap moves by >= 0.03 against U_full, or any rank flips; item Spearman < 0.85. If killed, R1 picks v1.1c if it passed its frozen rule. Otherwise R1 picks 'judge.v1 + decline subtraction', with U_dec and its CI printed in every row and the decline arm marked 'invalid as a floor, used as an offset'. U_CU is then never quoted.

statement: FACTPRESENT's null on real items (cell a, -0.010, n 10) is a rubric-coverage effect, not a reading failure. Real v0.1 rubrics need several facts, and the single 'key fact' chunk covers at most 1 of k must-points. Pack-written self-tests are single-fact by construction. Prediction: (i) the share of an item's must_any/must_k points matched in the kept context predicts per-item U across K0/K1/K3; the pooled slope CI excludes 0 and the slope is at least +0.15 U per unit share. (ii) The median must-point coverage of the gold chunk is at most 0.5 on real items and at least 0.9 on the topical self-tests.
why_now: ORACLE-REAL is about to report a reading ceiling. Without this decomposition, a null there cannot tell 'the 1.7B cannot read' apart from 'one chunk cannot answer a multi-point rubric'. That difference decides the page wording before 10-23.
method: Freeze the criterion (sha) first. Reuse FACTPRESENT's matcher: v0.1 grading must_any/must_k with the precheck semantics, self-test in_pack_facts. Apply it per must-point instead of per item. Inputs: (a) the dumped K0/K1/K3 Context blocks from the FACTPRESENT replay tree, (b) the hand-labelled gold chunks in arms/oracle-real/gold-labels.tsv. Outputs: per-item must-point coverage share (kept context, gold chunk alone), joined to the existing Haiku 5.5-low U. Fit a mixed-effects or item-clustered bootstrap slope of U on coverage share over MAIN 97 x 3 arms, and over the 180 self-tests apart. Report the gold-chunk coverage distribution, real vs self-test. When ORACLE-REAL lands, split its per-item lift by gold-chunk coverage (at most 0.5 vs above 0.5). 0 LLM, 0 judge.
cost: 0 LLM, 0 judge, 0 paid; about 2-3 h of scripting on the MacBook over existing replay dumps and judgments.
ceiling: n/a (0-LLM analysis). It decides whether the pack claim may say 'reading is the bottleneck' or 'one-chunk retrieval cannot satisfy multi-fact questions'.
kill_criterion: Kill the rubric-coverage explanation if the pooled slope CI includes 0, OR if the gold-chunk median coverage on real items is above 0.7, i.e. it is not materially lower than on the self-tests. The page then attributes the real-item null to reading or distractors, and ORACLE-REAL alone carries the reading claim.
lens: Packs and the RAG funnel. Wher

statement: a competitor team's 0-10 holistic ratio-of-sums rubric (the RIVALSET port: Claude grader, Opus+web reference) gives a bare refusal and a hedged non-answer >= 0.15 of the reference. Their 65 pct would then be floor-inclusive like our raw ratio (always-decline raw 0.306 under judge.v1), not comparable in kind to U. Planned presentation: a three-column 'what each number includes' table (floor, grader family, item exposure) and no delta.
why_now: The research page must place a competitor team's 65 pct next to our ruler. Today we can only assert, from the rubric text, that it 'keeps the grader's floor'. One measured floor turns that assertion into a number a sceptic can check. RIVALSET's level port failed G0, so the floor is reported as a ratio within the port, not as an absolute.
method: Freeze a criterion first. Pick 30 of their 72 public questions with a seeded sample. Use the RIVALSET port prompt and their recorded references unchanged. Grade the frozen FLOOR decline texts (a) bare refusal, (b) hedged and (c) fluent no-content (same wording, question substituted) with Haiku 5.5-low, N 4: 90 calls. Grade their own recorded answers on the same 30 under the same Haiku grader (30 calls) as the in-port reference level. Report the decline / reference sum ratio and decline / a competitor team-answer ratio with bootstrap CIs. No generation; nothing from blind/ or v0.4.
ceiling: Decides one table line of the claim (how the competitor number is presented). It is a level estimate with a narrow CI at n 30, so MDE does not apply.
kill_criterion: If the bare-refusal ratio CI high is < 0.05, their scale is effectively floor-free. The page then drops the floor caveat and presents their 65 pct as 'raw-like in kind; differs from our ruler in items (public, iterated dev set), grader family (Claude on Claude) and single grading', still with no delta. If it is >= 0.15, the page prints the measured refusal floor next to their number and next to our raw 0.306. Between 0.05 and 0.15, the page prints the floor with its CI and no adjective.

statement: A reason-code subset of hidden answers exists whose reveal is net-useful: correct:CE >= 1.0 and no health-tagged CE. Example: warned but cited, first content sentence cited, health excluded, all-citations-removed excluded. If so, show-anyway can be kept for that subset only, with health never revealable. The current all-hidden button returns 7 correct, 35 CE and 59 partial per 100 (SHOWANYWAY, kill met).
why_now: HON-2 killed show-anyway as specified, but the note still has to say what the button does by 10-23. 'Remove it' costs +0.104 floor-adjusted U of partial content. A rule chosen on LP and confirmed on MINI is a 0-cost, freezable fix. WARNSPEC v2's tiers (no-source / beyond-source / sourced) and the RU reason codes are already in the receipts.
method: 0-LLM, select-then-confirm. Freeze the criterion and the candidate list first: at most 6 reason-code subsets from WARNSPEC tiers and RU hide reasons, with health always excluded. Select on LP (LITEPACKS K0/K1/K3 x 277) the subset with the best correct:CE that keeps >= 15 % of revealable rows. Confirm on MINI (null-cal pool controls, untouched by selection) with the same frozen rule. Also report per-tier for the 4B traces if HON-7 runs. Same script family as HON-2.
ceiling: A note-wording decision. On MINI, correct:CE at about 60-100 revealed rows gives a CI of roughly +-0.3, enough to separate >= 1.0 from the pooled 0.19.
kill_criterion: If no pre-listed subset reaches correct:CE >= 1.0 on LP with >= 15 % of revealable rows, or the selected subset's MINI correct:CE has CI-high < 1.0, or it contains any health CE, the note recommends show-anyway behind a second confirmation with 'unverified, often wrong' for non-health only, and removal for health (the HON-2 fallback). statement: On the 20 REFVAR dev ids, swapping the reference family (Claude Opus+web vs Codex+web, uncapped) changes U by <= 0.03 under each judge family. The judge x reference interaction (same-family cell minus cross-family cell) is also <= 0.03. The judge-family offset (Codex about +0.10 vs Claude) holds in every cell. If so, the R4 headline can be the spec's min over judge families, averaged over the two references, with the 2x2 printed as a sensitivity table. If not, the same-family lift (arXiv 2609.17857, 3.4-8.4 pp) acts inside our ratio and the headline must come from per-cell numbers.
why_now: R3 generates both v0.4 reference families on 10-22, and R4 scores on 10-24. The 2x2 is the only defence against a sceptic's 'Claude grades Claude', and it is the same flaw we point out in a competitor team's 65 pct. We must know the expected size of the interaction on dev before the spec fixes how the 2x2 enters the headline. REFVAR measured only Claude references under a Claude judge.
method: Freeze a criterion first. r4to has Codex write one uncapped web reference draw on the 20 REFVAR ids, using the reference.r3-pilot prompt unchanged (20 generations, dev only). Haiku 5.5-low judge.v1 (or the RV1 rule) judges the existing 1.7B and 4B traces against the Codex reference: 20 x 2 arms x 2 orders, N 4, about 80 calls. Combine with the existing REFVAR Claude-reference rows. r4to runs the Codex judge on all four cells (about 160 calls). Compute per-cell U, the paired reference-family dU per judge, and the interaction with a cluster bootstrap over items. If Codex is not available by 10-22 night, run the Claude-judge column only and state the Codex column as unmeasured.
cost: about 80 Haiku; about 20 Codex generations + 160 Codex judge calls (r4to, about 1 h); 0 Opus; 0 paid
ceiling: The published same-family lift is 0.034-0.084. Paired MDE at n 20 x 2 arms is about 0.035 (REFVAR half-widths 0.017-0.02), so the upper half of the published range is detectable.
kill_criterion: If the interaction is >= 0.03 with a CI excluding 0, or any reference-family dU is >= 0.03 under one judge, the R2 spec computes the headline as the min over all four (judge, reference) cells (not reference-averaged) and prints the 2x2 in the headline row. The competitor row is then labelled with the measured same-family lift. If both are < 0.03 and the CIs include 0, keep the spec section 3.2 average and print the 2x2 as sensitivity only.

statement: Even under the ORACLE-REAL per-item lift, the best feasible keep-step rescue cannot move MAIN 97 by MDE. The rescue moves S3 'dense candidate not picked' items (10 of 17) into the kept context under the same work budget. Expected dU = (number of S3 items the rescue puts in the kept context) x (ORACLE-REAL mean per-item lift, its CI upper bound) / 97 stays below 0.03. Further keep/dense engineering is then closed for the 10-25 submission.
why_now: RAG-FUNNEL names S3 as the top lever, with a +0.025 self-test prior. The real-item prior from FACTPRESENT is about 0. Once ORACLE-REAL reports, this one product decides whether any keep-step arm is worth a mini slot before the 10-23 freeze. It stops a ninth retrieval arm from being built on the self-test prior.
method: Freeze the criterion before ORACLE-REAL results are read: formula, the candidate rescue rules, the budget. Using the RAG-FUNNEL replay (stub server, logging patch, 0 generation), replay 3 pre-declared budget-neutral keep rules on K3 MAIN 97 and v0.1: R1 dense top-3 replacing the lowest-cosine appended chunk, R2 dense-first ordering of the existing appends, R3 V1orC with tau 0.65. These are reach measurements only, not new arms. For each rule, count S3->kept transitions and S4/S5->dropped regressions (kept-title diff). Compute expected dU with the ORACLE-REAL lift (point and CI upper bound), and with the FACTPRESENT real cell (a) as the pessimistic prior. 0 LLM, 0 judge.
cost: 0 LLM, 0 judge; MacBook replay about 15 min per rule, plus 1 h of analysis. It depends on ORACLE-REAL finishing (same day).
ceiling: Perfect-fix S3 ceiling +0.115, self-test prior +0.025, real prior about 0. The analysis checks whether the best realistic rule times the measured lift clears 0.03 at n 97.
kill_criterion: If the best rule's expected dU, using the ORACLE-REAL CI upper bound, is below 0.03: close the keep/dense line for 10-25 and write 'retrieval reach is not the binding constraint on real items' on the page. If it is at least 0.03 AND the rule regresses at most 1 S5 item: the rule (one rule only) gets a frozen 1.7B K3 MAIN screen, Haiku N=4, on divergent-main.ids. Any other outcome: no screen.
